newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Three more firms seek Bucharest bourse listing.
newsitem.headline: Three more firms seek Bucharest bourse listing.

text.p: The Bucharest bourse said on Friday another three companies had applied for a listing but it could not say when they would begin trading.

State companies Grimex, a mining equipment manufacturer, Industria Sarmei SA, which produces steel and steel wire, and Maralact SA, a milk processing company had taken to 14 the number of firms which have applied for a quotation on the second tier, the bourse said.

Bursa de Valori Bucuresti, which opened last November, now trades 13 stocks, all on the second tier. Only one of them is privately held. Another three state companies are listed but their shares do not trade.
The exchange could not say when any of the 14 listing applicants would have its shares traded.

"The listing process is rather lengthy. Newcomers have to put together a file, win a bourse committee listing approval, sign a contract with the exchange and only then they can go into trading. It may take a while," a bourse official said.

The bourse also plans to hold public offers for 14 firms including a brewer, a medicine producer, a pulp and paper factory, as well as the national travel operator ONT Carpati SA and the country's sole newsprint maker Letea SA.

Brokers hail the bourse moves as apt to boost liquidity on the exchange which has seen sluggish activity in recent months. They say institutional investors, so far almost absent from trading will step in for fresh stocks.
"With the OTC market's opening near, the bourse should do something to attract bigger investors," a broker said.
An over-the-counter (OTC) system is now undergoing tests and is scheduled to go into trading by the end of this month. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
